Title: Transform Graphic (2D)
Content: Transform Graphic(2D) - Scale, rotate or move Graphics in the 2D window. - Select the Transform Graphic(2D) tool from the 2D toolbar. - Or, navigate to and select Main Menu Materials Graphics Transform Graphic(2D) Scale Graphics - Select the Transform Graphic(2D) tool from the 2D toolbar. - Select the Graphic to be edited in the 2D window. The Graphic Gizmo will appear. - Click and drag the arrow of the Graphic Gizmo to scale the selected Graphic, maintaining the height and width ratio. - When the desired size is achieved, release the mouse. - Navigate to the Property Editor Graphic Transformation Width or Height to adjust the graphic's dimension (For detailed information, please refer to Edit Texture.) Rotate Graphics - Select the Transform Graphic(2D) tool from the 2D toolbar. - Select the Graphic to be edited in the 2D window. The Graphic Gizmo will appear. - Click and drag the dotted circle of the Graphic Gizmo to rotate the selected Graphic. - When the Graphic is rotated as desired, release the mouse. Move Graphics - Select the Transform Graphic(2D) tool from the 2D toolbar. - Click and drag the Graphic to move. - When the Graphic is moved as desired, release the mouse.

Title: Edit 3D Pen (Avatar)
Content: List of Contents Select/Move Delete Objective Edit lines created on an Avatar. Location Main Menu 3D Garment Edit 3D Pen (Avatar) 3D Toolbar Edit 3D Pen (Avatar) Operation Select/Move Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu 3D Garment Edit 3D Pen (Avatar) 3D Toolbar Edit 3D Pen (Avatar) If a Garment is on the Avatar, the Garment appears translucent. Click on the line or the shape to be selected. The line or the shape is selected and highlighted in yellow. While the line of the shape is selected, click and drag to move the selected item to the desired position. Delete Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu 3D Garment Edit 3D Pen (Avatar) 3D Toolbar Edit 3D Pen (Avatar) If a Garment is on the Avatar, the Garment appears translucent. Select the line or the shape to be deleted. Right click on the selected item and select Delete or hit the Delete key on the keyboard. The selected line or shape is deleted. Note: To select multiple lines or shapes, hold down the Shift-key on the keyboard, then click on additional lines or shapes. To select all lines and shapes on the Avatar, hit the Ctrl+A on the keyboard. After the lines and shapes are drawn on the Avatar, if you delete the Avatar, all previously created lines and shapes are also deleted.

Title: [Popup] Show/Hide Puckering
Content: Objective Show or hide all Puckering. Location 3D Window Garment Show/Hide Icon (Mouse Over) Show Puckering Operation Follow the indicated guideline below: 3D Window Garment Show/Hide Icon (Mouse Over) Show Puckering All created Puckering is now being hidden. Follow the indicated guideline again. All hidden Puckering is now being displayed again.

Title: [Tool] Edit Puckering
Content: Objective Edit location and length of Puckering segments. Location Main Menu Materials Puckering Edit Puckering 2D Toolbar Edit Puckering Operation Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu Materials Puckering Edit Puckering 2D Toolbar Edit Puckering Click on Puckering Drag to locate. To adjust the length of Puckering, click one of the two end points of the Puckering and drag to adjust to the desired length. The selected Puckering is now being adjusted.

Title: Create .HW File and Register .LCN File
Content: Operation Click on the circled area to fully display the Login window. Check or uncheck the circled areas according to the image below, then click on Create HW File. Note: When creating file, save the file name as your user ID. Send the newly created .HW file to support@clo3d.com, for a .LCN file request. Download the .LCN file received from the CLO Support Team. Check or uncheck the circled areas according to the image below, then click on Register LCN File. Once the .LCN file is registered and below message appears, click OK to go back to the Login window. Double check on the check-boxes' status and the 'Registered' message with a check icon below the Register LCN File button, then click Log In to run the the program.

Title: Edit Piping Length
Content: Objective Edit the length of Piping. Location Main Menu Materials Piping Edit Piping 3D Toolbar Edit Piping Operation Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu Materials Piping Edit Piping 3D Toolbar Edit Piping An editable line appears on top of all Piping, and also a hidden Piping appears in semi-transparent temporarily. Click and drag on either end points of the editable line to adjust the length.

Title: [Property] Set Sublayer
Content: Objective Assign orders to the Sewing Lines on a Pattern which folds on itself such as seam allowances and pleats in order to increase simulation stability. Location Main Menu Sewing Edit Sewing 2D Toolbar Edit Sewing Operation Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu Sewing Edit Sewing 2D Toolbar Edit Sewing All established Sewing Lines appear in the 2D window. Select the Sewing Lines to set Sublayer. Sewing Line properties appear in the property editor. Toggle on the Set Sublayer option. A red arrow which indicates the order of the selected pair of Sewing Lines appear. Note: The half of the seam next to the arrow head is fixed and the other half next to the arrow tail moves according to the setting. Change the Sublayer setting as needed. Reverse Direction Swap the fixed Sewing Line and the moving Sewing Line. Front Back Decide which side of the fabric is attached to the fixed Sewing Line. Activate Simulation. Changes are applied respective to the setting.

Title: [Popup] Activate/Deactivate Sewing Lines
Content: Objective Activate or deactivate Sewing Lines as needed. Use this function when Sewing Lines should be applied after garment is draped such as the back slits for a men's jacket. Location 2D Toolbar Edit Sewing Right Click Pop-Up Menu (on Sewing Line) Deactivate/Activate Sewing (Selected) Object Browser Scene Tab Right Click Pop-Up Menu (on Item) Deactivate/Activate Sewing (Selected) Operation Follow the indicated guideline below: 2D Toolbar Edit Sewing Right Click Pop-Up Menu (on Sewing Line) Deactivate/Activate Sewing (Selected) Object Browser Scene Tab Right Click Pop-Up Menu (on Item) Deactivate/Activate Sewing (Selected) Deactivated Sewing Lines appear in white in the 2D and the 3D window and their names appear in dark grey in the Scene Tab.

Title: Create/Delete Reference Line
Content: List of Contents Create Delete Objective Create Reference Line as needed to check its original shape when editing the Pattern. Location Main Menu 2D Pattern Edit Transform Pattern 2D Toolbar Transform Pattern Operation Create Click the tool/menu indicated. Right-click on the pattern for which you want to create a reference line, and then click the Clone as Reference Line menu. Modify the pattern. You can check the shape of the original pattern as a reference line. Delete Click the tool/menu indicated. Right-click on the pattern where you want to delete the reference line, and then click the Delete Reference Line menu. The created Reference Line is deleted. Note: Select Reference line with Trace tool to trace as internal line/shape. (ver 7.2 )

Title: Add Arrangement Point
Content: Objective Add new Arrangement Point on the Bound Volume as needed. Note: Without corresponding Bounding Volume, the Arrangement Point is invisible. Location Main Menu Avatar Avatar Editor Arrangement Arrangement Point Add Operation Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu Avatar Avatar Editor Arrangement Arrangement Point Add A new arrangement point called "Arrangement Point" is now being created at the bottom of the A-Point list in the Arrangement tab, and its properties appear in the Property Editor. Set details for Arrangement Point. Name Changes the name of the Arrangement Point. Arrangement Arrangement BV Selects the Bounding Volume where the Arrangement Point to be placed. X Moves the Arrangement Point left and right. Y Moves the Arrangement Point up and down. Offset Sets the distance between the Avatar and the Arrangement Point. Wrap Direction The direction in which the Pattern wrapped around the Avatar. Note: Symmetric Arrangement Point Setting Name the Arrangement Point with an underscore and location (R for right and L for left) at the end of the name to set Symmetric Arrangement Point. The name must be the same as the name before the underscore and the alphabet. All arrangement points apart from the Avatar's body are symmetrically set by default from CLO Enterprise 3.0 (ver3.0). _R _L Follow the indicated steps below to save the Avatar and Arrangement Points, and reload to apply the setting. Light-blue outer line appears around the Symmetric Arrangement Point. Save Avatar: Main Menu File Save as Avatar Save Arrangement Point: Main Menu Avatar Avatar Editor Arrangement Arrangement Point Save

Title: Extend/Trim & Add Point to Pattern Outline or Internal Line
Content: Objective Extend or trim Internal Lines to its surrounding Pattern outline or extend or trim Internal Lines and add points to Pattern outline or other Internal Lines(ver 6.0). Location Main Menu 2D Pattern Edit Edit Pattern 2D Toolbar Edit Pattern Operation Select the tool/menu indicated in Location. Right-Click on an Internal Line or Point. The pop-up menu appears. Click Extend/Trim &amp Add Point To Pattern Outline/To Internal Line(ver 6.0) The Selected point is extended to the Pattern Outline or Internal Line and Points are added at the same time.

Title: Delete Tape Measure
Content: Objective Delete tape measures that are no longer in need. Location Main Menu Avatar Avatar Editor Measure Delete Operation Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu Avatar Avatar Editor Measure Delete Select a tape measure to delete. Click on the Delete icon. The selected tape measure is now being deleted.

Title: Smooth Curve
Content: Objective Round the corner of Patterns and Internal Shapes (ver2.3.0). Location Main Menu 2D Pattern Edit Smooth Curve 2D Toolbar Smooth Curve Operation Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu 2D Pattern Edit Smooth Curve 2D Toolbar Smooth Curve Click and drag a corner or a curved segment to be rounded. The selected corner/curved segment is rounded/edited. Right click on the mouse while dragging the point or the curved segment (ver2.4.0). The Round Corner by Length window appears. Enter the desired line length and curvature. Then, click OK. The selected corner/curved segment is rounded/edited.

Title: Windows - CLO Network Version Installation
Content: Objective Install Windows - CLO Network Version. Any Asset downloaded in the previous version is maintained when a new version is installed (ver5.0.0.) Operation Run the DVD received upon purchase or the install file received via email. After running the install file, press "Next" on the setup window to continue installation. Review the License Agreement and click "I Agree" to accept the terms of the agreement. Choose a location to install the program. Select a Start Menu folder. The product begins installing. It takes less than a minute. After the installation is completed, click "Finish" to close the window. Once the program has finished installation, a Server must be set up. Click the link below and check to see if the Sentinel Admin Control Center screen shows up, as it does on the picture below: ACC Page If the following screen does not appear, the HASP Driver must be reinstalled: Manual Sentinel HASP Driver Installation As shown below, click on the "Configuration" menu on left of the ACC Page. Select "Access to Remote License Managers" as below image. Check the "Aggressive Search for Remote Licenses" item as shown below. Enter the IP address of the Server PC in the "Specify Search Parameters" item. Click the "Submit" button. If the HASP Key can be seen as shown below after approximately 10 seconds, then the configuration is successful. Note: Identifying Server PC's IP Address Start (Windows) Button All Programs Accessories Command Prompt Enter 'ipconfig' or enter 'cmd' in the 'Run' menu Enter 'ipconfig' Reference site: http://www.ghacks.net/2011/05/17/network-troubleshooting-basics-the-ipconfig-command/

Title: Slider/Puller/Stopper OBJ Registration
Content: Create OBJ Register OBJ Objective Register your own OBJ file as a Slider/Puller/Stopper. Location Main Menu Materials Zipper Register OBJ Property Editor Shape Operation Create OBJ Check the requirements below when making OBJs in other 3D programs. Essential Set the name of the MESH to Slider and Puller when creating an OBJ with a slider and a puller. For each type, adjust the position to suit the meaning of the axis. (If the position of the axis is not correct, the OBJ may not be loaded in the correct position) Slider X-Axis Position the shoulder of the slider where zipper teeth insert on the X-axis 0. Y-Axis The direction the slider moves is the Y-axis, Position center of the slider where the center of the zipper teeth aligned at 0 of the Y-axis. Z-Axis Position the Z-axis 0 where the side of the zipper teeth is located. Stopper The stopper configured on both sides must be made to be the same scale as the two OBJ axes. X-Axis Position the shoulder of the slider where zipper teeth insert on the X-axis 0. Y-Axis Top Stopper Position the point where the most end (top) of the zipper blade is in contact with the Y-axis 0. Bottom Stopper When the slider is lowered all the way, the point where it touches the bottom of the slider is positioned on the Y-axis at 0. Z-Axis Position the Z-axis 0 where the side of the zipper teeth is located. Puller Place the position where the slider is attached at the origin (0,0,0). Note: The puller position is adjustable within the CLO. Slider &amp Puller Create sliders &amp pullers are created based on the slider axis. Register OBJ Select the tool/menu indicated in Location. The OBJ registration window appears. After setting the following options, click the OK button. Basic Type Select the type (Slider, Puller, Stopper, Slider &amp Puller) to register the OBJ. Name Enter a file name. Scale Adjust the size of the OBJ. Axis Conversion Change each axis of the OBJ. File OBJ Slider / Puller Load the OBJ file you want to register. Stopper (Top, Bottom-Open) Load each Top and Botton-Open OBJ file. The first OBJ loaded is placed in the direction of the zipper created first. Slider &amp Puller (ver 6.2) Load a combined zipper OBJ file. Select and assign the mesh item of Slider and Puller in the Select Mesh menu. Preview Check the imported OBJ file in advance. Puller Position Adjust the sliders on the X, Y, and Z axes to set where the puller is attached. Note: This setting is for Slider and Slider &amp Puller types only. The object is saved in the path below: Assets Materials Hardware_and_Trims Zipper Each object's folder

Title: Avatar Measure (ver 6.0)
Content: List of Contents Basic/Surface Circumference Measure Basic/Surface/Linear Measure Height Measure Objective Measure the circumference, length and height of the Avatar. Two methods are provided. Either based on the protruding part of the avatar or based on the surface of the curvature. Location Main Menu Avatar Measurement 3D Toolbar Click and hold down the Basic Circumference Measure Operation Basic/Surface Circumference Measure. Select the tool/menu indicated in Location. Click the starting point to be measured and click the second point in the desired direction. A Basic/Surface Circumference measure is displayed. Click once more when it is in the target shape. A Basic/Surface Circumference measure is created and the length is displayed. Basic/Surface/Linear Measure Select the tool/menu indicated in Location. Click the start point to be measured and double-click the end point. A Basic/Surface/Linear Tape Measure is created and its length is displayed. A Linear Measure runs through the Avatar by connecting the start and end points in a straight line. (ver 6.0) Height Measure Select the tool/menu indicated in Location. Click the point to be measured. A Height Measure that runs vertically from the clicked point to the ground is created and the length is displayed. Note: Hold down the Shift key on the keyboard to create vertical/horizontal/45 tilt. Use Attach to Measure tool to attach the pattern outline or Internal Line to the Avatar Measure.

Title: Shirring (ver5.1.0)
Content: Objective Express shirring realistically by reducing mesh size of the particular area of the Pattern. Location 2D Toolbar Edit Pattern Select a Line Property Editor Selected Line Shirring Operation Click on a Pattern Outline using the Transform Pattern tool or Edit Pattern tool. Follow the indicated path below: Property Editor Selected Line Shirring Click to toggle on the check box. Shirring is applied to the selected line and the shirring symbol appears on the 2D Pattern. The result can be checked on the 3D Garment or on the 2D Pattern after switching the 2D Pattern Rendering Style to Mesh. Adjust the Interval and Height of the Shirring. Interval Adjust the distance between each mesh. Height Adjust the Height of the Shirring. Note: Shirring is applied symmetrically when it is applied to Symmetric Patterns.

Title: Sewing Tension
Content: Sewing Tension - Adjust sewing Tension to improve 3D Garments fit. - Select the Edit Sewing tool from the 2D toolbar. - Select the Sewing Line which the sewing Tension needs to be adjusted. - Selected Sewing Lines properties appear in the Property Editor. Strength : Type in a value to adjust selected Sewing Lines Tension Strength. Ratio : Adjust the Tension Ratio to express how various types of Sewing method influence garment drapes. Note: The maximum Tension Ratio is 200%.

Title: Slider Gizmo
Content: List of Contents Move Rotate Objective Move or rotate slider to adjust its distance from zipper tape. Location Main Menu 3D Garment Select/Move 3D Toolbar Select/Move Operation Move Create a zipper. While the Simulation is turned off, follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu 3D Garment Select/Move 3D Toolbar Select/Move Click the slider. The slider is selected and its Gizmo appears. Click and drag the blue segment of the Gizmo to move the slider back and forth. Sliders cannot be moved along with Y and Z axes. Rotate With the Select/Move tool, click on the slider to access the Slider Gizmo. Click and drag the blue circle of the Gizmo to rotate on Y axis. Click and drag the yellow-green circle of the Gizmo to rotate on X axis. Click and drag the red circle of the Gizmo to rotate on Z axis. The selected zipper slider rotates based on the selected circle. To rotate the puller only, click on the puller while the slider is selected. The selected puller is highlighted in yellow and the Gizmo changes accordingly. Rotate the puller referencing #2. Note: To reset slider's position and angle, right click on the slider and select Reset Slider Arrangement option.

Title: Edit 3D Pen (Garment)
Content: List of Contents Select/Move Delete Objective Edit lines created on 3D Garments. Location 3D Toolbar Edit 3D Pen (Garment) Operation Select/Move Follow the indicated guideline below: 3D Toolbar Edit 3D Pen (Garment) Click the desired segment. The selected segment is highlighted in yellow and its length appears (ver5.0.0.) To edit, click and drag either end points of the segment to the desired place. The selected point is moved. The segment's length appears when it is selected (ver5.0.0.) Delete Right click on the point or segment to be deleted and select the Delete option, or hit the Delete key on the keyboard. The selected point or line is deleted.

Title: Register Custom OBJ as Button
Content: Create Button OBJ Register Button OBJ Create Button OBJ by Thread Type Objective Register a custom OBJ file as Button. Location Main Menu Materials Button Register Button Property Editor Shape Operation Create Button OBJ Please check below requirements before registering an OBJ as a button. Required: ℹ From CLO 7.3, no 1, 2 requirements are not necessary and can be set at registration. Position the face of an OBJ towards Y-axis. Position the contact point of an OBJ where it should be attached to 3D garments at 0,0,0 (x,y,z) coordinates. The unit of OBJs must be in mm. e.g.) Please check the attached OBJ file in your 3D modeling program for better understanding. Recommended: Please maintain the number of vertices of an OBJ below 1000 to avoid speed issues. The distance between an OBJ and the ground should be 0. (You can adjust the distance in CLO. Button Property Setting Thread Length (cm)) Register Button OBJ Select the tool/menu indicated in Location. Register Button window appears. After setting the following options, Click OK. Property Description Basic Set the name of the button file. File Size If the OBJ shape is different for each button size, click the + button on the top right to register as buttons of various sizes. Size Name Set the size name. OBJ Load the OBJ file to be registered with the button. Select Mesh (ver 7.3) Set the mesh for the buttons and thread. OBJ Load the OBJ file to be registered with the button. Width/Thickness /Weight Set the width/thickness/weight of the button. Set as Default Set the size to be applied by default when changing with the button. Axis Conversion (ver 7.3) Switch axis of OBJ files in real time. Preview (ver 7.3) The imported OBJ file will be previewed. The registered button is saved in the path below. CLO Assets Materials Hardware_and_Trims Button &amp Buttonhole Button Create Button OBJ by Thread Type Set the name of the OBJ file for each thread type to *_Cross.obj, *_Parallel.obj , *_Square.obj. Register the created OBJ file as a button. Save the created *_Cross.btn, *_Parallel.btn , *_Square.btn files in the path below. C:UsersPublicDocumentsCLOAssetsMaterialsHardware_and_TrimsButton &amp ButtonholeButton Run CLO and change the type of the thread in the button property window &gt Type &gt Thread Type.

Title: Transform Graphic (3D)
Content: Transform Graphic (3D) - Scale, rotate or move Graphics in the 3D window. - Select the Transform Graphic (3D) tool from the 3D toolbar. - Or, navigate to and select Main Menu Material Graphics Transform Graphic (3D) Scale Graphics - Select the Transform Graphic (3D) tool from the 3D toolbar. - Select the Graphic to be edited in the 3D window. The Graphic Gizmo will appear. - Click and drag the arrow of the Graphic Gizmo to scale the selected Graphic. - When the desired size is achieved, release the mouse. - Navigate to the Property Editor Graphic Transformation Width or Height to adjust the graphic's dimension (For detailed information, please refer to Edit Texture.) Rotate Graphics - Select the Transform Graphic (3D) tool from the 3D toolbar. - Select the Graphic to be edited in the 3D window. The Graphic Gizmo will appear. - Click and drag the dotted circle of the Graphic Gizmo to rotate the selected Graphic. - When the Graphic is rotated as desired, release the mouse. Move Graphics - Select the Transform Graphic (3D) tool from the 3D toolbar. - Click and drag the Graphic to move. - When the Graphic is moved as desired, release the mouse.

Title: Slash and Spread
Content: List of Contents Slash and Spread Create Slash Line Rotate Pattern Slash and Spread - Create a Slash Line inside a Pattern to divide, rotate, and edit the Pattern. - Select the Slash&ampSpread tool from the 2D toolbar. - Or, navigate to the Main Menu and select 2D Patterns Edit Slash&ampSpread. Create Slash Line - To divide and rotate the Patterns, the Slash Line must be created first. - The Slash Line can be created on the Pattern outlines. - Click on the Pattern outline to create the start point. The start point of the Slash Line will be the fiducial point where the Pattern will rotated on the basis of. Drag the mouse on click again on the Pattern outline to complete the Slash Line. - Baselines and Internal Lines can also be used as Slash Lines. Rotate Pattern - Click the half of the Pattern that will be rotated. Hover the mouse over the half and when the Pattern is highlighted in light-blue, click to select. When the half of the Pattern is selected, it will be highlighted in yellow. - Move the mouse cursor to preview the Pattern after the modification. Rotate the Pattern to spread or clip Patterns. - Move the half of the Pattern as desired and click to complete the modification. - Baselines and Internal Lines can also be used to rotate Patterns. - Or, when moving the half of the Pattern, right-click to access the Spread window. Enter the desired values to Distance and Angle and click OK.

Title: Select
Content: List of Contents Select Transform Pattern Tool Edit Pattern Tool Pattern Properties Deselect Select Multiple Patterns Select/Move Tool Select All Select - Select patterns in the 2D and 3D windows. - Select the Transform Pattern tool or the Edit Pattern tool from the 2D toolbar. - Select the Select/Move tool from the 3D toolbar. Transform Pattern Tool Select with Clicks - Select the Transform Pattern tool from the 2D toolbar. - Hover over the pattern to be selected as its outline will be highlighted in light-blue. - Click on the pattern. The Selected pattern will be highlighted in yellow. Lasso Selection - Double click on the 2D window to activate the Lasso Selection. - Click around the pattern to be selected to create the Lasso Selection. - Click the start point again to complete. - Patterns encompassed within the Lasso Selection will be selected and highlighted in yellow. - The patterns must be fully enclosed in the Lasso Selection to be properly selected. Edit Pattern Tool Select with Clicks - Select the Edit Pattern tool from the 2D toolbar. - With the Edit Pattern tool, points and segments can be selected. Double click the point or the segment to select the entire pattern. Lasso Selection - Double click on the 2D window to activate the Lasso Selection. - Click around the pattern to be selected to create the Lasso Selection. - Click the start point again to complete. - Patterns encompassed within the Lasso Selection will be selected and highlighted in yellow. - The patterns must be fully enclosed in the Lasso Selection to be properly selected. Pattern Properties - When the pattern is selected, its properties will appear in the Property Editor. Deselect - Click on the 2D window to Deselect Patterns. - Originally selected patterns will no longer be highlighted in yellow. Select Multiple Patterns - To select multiple patterns, points, or segments, hold down the Shift key on the keyboard and select the items to be selected. Select/Move Tool - Select the Select/Move tool from the 3D toolbar. - Click on the 3D pattern to select and click on the 3D window to deselect. - To select more than one patterns, hold down the Shift key on the keyboard and click on patterns to be selected. Select All - To select all patterns in the 2D window, click and drag to encompass them with the marquee box. - Or, hit the Ctrl+A keys on the keyboard to select all patterns in both 2D and 3D windows. - When you hit the Ctrl+A keys while the Edit Sewing tool is activated, all sewing lines will be selected. - Likewise, when you hit the Ctrl+A keys while the Select/Move Button tool is activated, all buttons will be selected in the 3D window.

Title: Trace as / Convert to Internal Shape
Content: Objective Use the Trace function to convert selected lines/shapes or areas into Internal Lines/Shapes. Location 3D Toolbar Edit 3D Pen (Garment) Operation Follow the indicated guideline below: 3D Toolbar Edit 3D Pen (Garment) Click on created Baselines or Internal Lines on 3D Garment. The selected Baselines or Internal Lines are now being highlighted in yellow color. Right-click on the selected Baselines or Internal Lines. A Pop-up menu appears. Select Trace as Internal Shape or Convert to Internal Shape in the pop-up menu. The selected Baselines or Internal Lines are now being traced as /converted to Internal Shapes.

Title: Rearrange Tape Measure
Content: Objective Rearrange tape measure according to avatar size. Location Main Menu Avatar Avatar Editor Measure Fit to Avatar Operation Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu Avatar Avatar Editor Measure Fit to Avatar Click on the Fit to Avatar icon. Tape measures are now being rearranged automatically to the avatar's size.

Title: [Tool] Segment Puckering
Content: Objective Apply puckering to Pattern's external/internal lines. Location Main Menu Materials Puckering Segment Puckering 2D Toolbar Segment Puckering Operation Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu Materials Puckering Segment Puckering 2D Toolbar Segment Puckering Click on a segment to apply Puckering. Puckering is now being applied to the selected segment. Created puckering displays in the 3D window. Note: Click-and-drag on the 2D window to encompass all segments where Puckerings to be applied. Puckerings appear on all selected segments (ver3.2.0).

Title: [Popup] Delete Puckering
Content: Objective Delete unnecessary Puckering. Location Main Menu Materials Puckering Edit Puckering 2D Toolbar Edit Puckering Operation Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu Materials Puckering Edit Puckering 2D Toolbar Edit Puckering Right click on top of the Puckering segment and select Delete, or press Delete key on keyboard. The selected Puckering is now being deleted.

Title: Optimize All Curve Points
Content: Objective Optimize the number of curve points on the segments to ease the Pattern editing proces. Location Main Menu 2D Pattern Edit Pattern 2D Toolbar Edit Pattern Operation Click the tool indicated in Location. Right-click on the 2D Pattern Window and click the Optimize All Curve Points, or right-click on the lines to optimize the curve points and click the Optimize All Curve Points. Optimize Curve Points window appears, and the number of curve points is automatically applied as an optimized ratio. (ver 7.2) Adjust the ratio of curve points. Closer to 0%, there will be fewer curve points, but there may be deviations from the original curvature.

Title: [Popup] Show/Hide Sewing
Content: Objective When Sewing Lines are too complicated, hide them for clear view as needed. Location 2D Toolbar Edit Sewing Right Click Pop-Up Menu (on Sewing Line) Hide Sewing (Selected)/ Hide Sewing (All) Object Browser Right Click Pop-Up Menu (on Item) Hide Sewing (Selected)/ Hide Sewing (All) Operation Follow the indicated guideline below: 2D Toolbar Edit Sewing Right Click Pop-Up Menu (on Sewing Line) Hide Sewing (Selected)/ Hide Sewing (All) Object Browser Right Click Pop-Up Menu (on Item) Hide Sewing (Selected)/ Hide Sewing (All) The selected Sewing Lines or all Sewing Lines show or disappear from the 2D and the 3D window. Note 1: All Sewing Lines appear in the 2D window when the Edit Sewing tool is selected since the Show 2D Sewing tool is activated automatically. Note 2: 2D Window Show Sewing icon Show Sewing (ver5.0 or later)
